name: Facet
text: We should implement a dark theme by default with a light-theme toggle that remains visible at all times. This enhances overall visibility and reduces eye strain for users, especially in low-light environments, promoting clarity and enjoyment while using the interface. The trade-off is that some users who prefer a permanent light theme may have to adjust to toggling, but the benefits of a modern, visually appealing design outweigh this inconvenience.

name: Pane
text: The toggle’s real risk is habituation—users won’t switch even when glare or sunlight makes the dark theme worse. A context-aware theme that auto-adjusts to lighting would avoid this trap, but it fails in mixed lighting where sunlight hits one side of the screen. Settle it with A/B tests: measure task completion time and reported strain in both glare and low-light conditions.
